Jordan / Tom —

On initial inspection of the telemetry: the SummitPay dedicated pool is showing sustained queue depth increases on 3 of 6 instances. GPU utilization is near 98% on those nodes, and KV cache eviction rates spiked in line with the latency bump. There are also a handful of model retry errors tied to out-of-memory attempts for long-context requests (~>8k tokens).

Short-term mitigations we can apply now (non-disruptive, <15min):
- Temporarily enable model-variant fallback for SummitPay routes to a 16-bit quantized variant that reduces memory pressure (can be applied per-route).
- Increase per-customer concurrency limit by allowing a small burst up to +12% headroom on the pool (requires ops approval).
- Aggressive prefix/KV cache expiration for long contexts (reduce memory footprint)

I will push the fallback and cache-policy change immediately after confirmation from SummitPay on acceptable quality trade-offs. If you prefer, we can also spin up one additional node in the pool (30–45 min to provision on Dedicated) — that requires us to escalate capacity allocation internally.

I'll post back with the first triage findings in the bridge.

Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
